exposure: Maternal pre-pregnancy BMI (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese)
cohort: The study included 793 consecutive women with at term, uncomplicated deliveries, categorized by pre-pregnancy BMI into underweight (96), normal weight (551), overweight (107), and obese (39) groups.
finding: Pre-pregnancy underweight does not negatively impact the birth weight of healthy, term neonates when gestational weight gain is within the normal recommended range.
cross-section timing: Data was prospectively collected at the time of delivery.
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured at birth, with offspring of underweight women being comparable in size to normal weight women, but significantly lighter than those of overweight and obese women.
